title: Multilingual retrieval: lexical, dense and hybrid
scope: A small English/Portuguese seed benchmark over the existing bounded source library. Retrieval only; no generated answers or paid inference.

model.license: Base model MIT; ONNX export references the base model
model.pooling: Attention-masked mean pooling, L2 normalization; query: and passage: prefixes; 512-token truncation.
model.download_notice: Optional first-use download of about 136 MB of model/tokenizer files plus the runtime. Runs on your device; no query is sent to a model API.

runtime_parity.rule: Exact probe token IDs and cosine >= 0.99 on all three probes. This is a compatibility heuristic, not a retrieval-quality score. Native and browser q8 outputs are not assumed bit-identical.
runtime_parity.live_corpus: Re-encode passages and development questions in the browser; select browser abstention thresholds from development only. Do not mix native passage vectors with browser query vectors.

corpus.deduplication: Case, accents and punctuation normalized for exact-wording deduplication; first source retained. No rating classification inferred from a retrieved phrase.
corpus.license: Olist-derived excerpts CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; authored method documents MIT.

benchmark.annotation_status: AI-assisted, agent-authored seed questions and binary relevance judgments; not independently human-validated. Review and amend before claiming external benchmark quality.

audit_log.review: AI-assisted second-agent source/wording audit, conducted without consulting retrieval model scores; not independent human validation.
changes: Qualified nonreceipt as a statement at review-writing time, not proof a product never arrived.
Changed regression question to concepts explicitly stated in its relevant passage.
Clarified bilingual units and category IDs versus semantic independence.
audit_log.evaluation_protocol: Only source-fidelity wording and description corrected after initial scoring; no model, relevance IDs, threshold rule or development questions changed. Recomputed the frozen artifact once.

benchmark.split_rule: Authored category IDs are disjoint across development and test; this does not prove semantic independence. Bilingual counterparts stay together. Threshold selection reads development only.
benchmark.selection_note: All three predeclared methods are reported; none is promoted using test scores.

threshold_selection.objective: development balanced answerability accuracy; equal-objective ties prefer the larger threshold

passages.title: Machine learning method notes
passages.text: Late delivery classification compares a simple baseline with a learned model on a later temporal holdout. Accuracy can be misleading when late orders are uncommon. Read precision, recall, F1, ROC AUC, class balance, and the confusion matrix together when available. A model has no demonstrated advantage until its measured holdout result is compared with the baseline.

passages.title: Machine learning method notes
passages.text: Delivery-duration regression predicts a continuous number of days. Mean absolute error (MAE) is expressed in days and describes the average absolute prediction error. Root mean squared error (RMSE) gives larger errors greater weight. R squared compares squared error with a constant-mean reference; it can be negative. Report only metrics actually computed by this run.

passages.title: Machine learning method notes
passages.text: Temporal evaluation trains on earlier orders and holds out later orders. Fit preprocessing inside the training pipeline. Post-outcome reviews and delivered timestamps leak future information into order-time predictions. Hyperparameter choices require a validation set or inner time-aware cross-validation; a final holdout should stay untouched until evaluation.

passages.title: Machine learning method notes
passages.text: The default document retriever uses local TF-IDF lexical similarity and returns source-linked excerpts. It does not use semantic embeddings or a generative language model. Search quality should be evaluated with independently authored question/relevant-source pairs; citation presence alone does not prove an answer is supported.

passages.title: Machine learning method notes
passages.text: Model feature rankings describe predictive associations in the evaluated dataset. They cannot establish causal business drivers. Synthetic records can validate software behavior but cannot prove real commercial performance. Forecasting, recommendation models, streaming, and fine-tuning are future extensions unless their implementations and evaluations are present.

passages.title: Olist historical demonstration workspace
passages.text:
The workspace uses the historical Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset published by Olist: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce . The publisher's release announcement is https://www.kaggle.com/general/67613 . Preserve its CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 attribution and terms; the DataPilot code license does not replace the dataset license.

This is an offline demonstration using historical marketplace records. It is not a connection to a current Olist service or an endorsement by Olist. Source dates retain the source clock representation; no timezone was established from these files.

passages.title: Olist historical demonstration workspace
passages.text: Classification predicts whether an eligible delivered order arrived after its estimated calendar delivery date. Regression predicts observed days from purchase to delivery. Filtering to delivered orders excludes canceled and undelivered orders, so these results do not establish performance on every newly placed order. Inputs must be available at the stated prediction time. Review text, actual delivery time and rating are outcomes and must not be order-time prediction inputs.

passages.title: Olist historical demonstration workspace
passages.text:
Review text is Portuguese. The text classifier predicts a rating group from the comment: ratings 1–2 are called negative, 3 neutral, and 4–5 positive. These names are proxies defined by the recorded ratings; they are not independently annotated sentiment labels. A chronological holdout uses review answer timestamps. Vocabulary and IDF are fitted on training text only.

The review analysis keeps the earliest answered review per order, then excludes missing comments or invalid ratings. This means comment authors need not represent all customers. Complaint counts use overlapping keyword rules among low-rating comments. They describe matched phrases rather than measured root causes or validated topic classifications.

passages.title: Olist historical demonstration workspace
passages.text:
The public evidence library contains only a bounded selection of repeated short review phrases with contact/address patterns excluded. It is a demonstration retrieval corpus, not a representative or complete review archive. Answers should identify original Portuguese excerpts and their source; DataPilot does not claim to have independently verified customer statements.

Any separate example operations policy in this repository is authored fictional demonstration material. It is not an actual Olist refund, shipping, or customer-service policy. Do not merge those fictional policy statements into claims about Olist.

lexical_index.definition: Lowercase, NFKD accent removal, ASCII word unigrams; sublinear TF and smoothed IDF; L2 cosine. No translation or synonym expansion.

limitations: Questions and relevance judgments were authored with AI assistance and have not been independently human-validated. This is a seed evaluation for review, not a validated external benchmark.

The 40 questions represent 20 bilingual category pairs, not 40 independent units. Eight categories are development-only and twelve test-only; related policy/privacy themes can still occur across the splits.

The small source corpus and question set cannot establish broad retrieval quality or multilingual generalization. Test questions are only withheld from threshold selection, not a pristine external research test.
Binary relevance is based on the supplied source wording. Review statements are historical customer claims, not verified facts, and rating groups are not independent sentiment annotations.
Abstention thresholds are small-development-set heuristics, not calibrated probabilities. False positive retrieval and missed evidence remain possible.
RRF scores and cosine scores use different scales. A higher numeric score across methods does not imply higher confidence.

Live semantic search downloads third-party runtime/model files on explicit request; availability, device memory and bandwidth can limit use. Saved evaluation remains inspectable without downloading the model.
No cross-encoder reranker or generative LLM is implemented by this experiment.
